confirming.Proposed outcome: A Python 3 CLI named tally reads one or more explicitly named UTF-8 text files, counts whitespace-separated tokens using str.split(), and prints exactly one '<count> <path>' line per file in argument order. decided: A small Python word-counting CLI called tally counts words in explicitly named text files and prints predictable per-file counts, for local users.

tally is strictly read-only: never modify, create, or delete input files or other repository files at runtime. Use Python 3 standard library only. Accept one or more explicit UTF-8 text file paths; stdin is out of scope. Refuse directories with a plain stderr error. Words are whitespace-separated tokens using str.split(). Print exactly '<count> <path>' per file in argument order, with no total. No arguments or unreadable/invalid UTF-8 files produce a plain stderr error and exit 1; success exits 0. Tests use unittest with temporary files and verify counts, output, errors, and unchanged input bytes. No packaging or recursive traversal.
